items.title: 63475_Arnett Cobb oral history interview
items.q: I had Butch Ballard on drums, George Rhodes on piano... George Rhodes Rule came back... George is up there, one of the guilty parties, playing piano for me.

ctx.x: Who'd you have on rhythm then?
I had Butch Ballard on drums, George Rhodes on piano and Poor Jumpin' George Jones on -- I mean Walter Buchanan on bass. Poor George came in later.
Well, when you did go (inaudible)? did add Bootsy Wood and...

items.title: 63475_Arnett Cobb oral history interview
items.q: And the piano player was George Phil Joey Rhodes. Of course, here I am again, six pieces.

ctx.x: No, this was in the '50s, early '50s. But anyhow, I had six pieces with Bootie, me and Dave Page. Rhythm section was Joe Harris. Bass player -- what was his name? Walter Buchanan. And the piano player was George Phil Joey Rhodes. Of course, here I am again, six pieces. But he said it sounded like a mob, six pieces. And we're working opposite of Barnet, Charlie Barnet. And Charlie would come on and play,

and then we'd come on and play, and he said, you sound like a mob. So he gave me the name Arnett Cobb and the Mobb -- (Laughter) -- spelled with two Bs, M-o-b-b. And he was the one that was instrumental in getting me in Birdland.
